concerns: The national preference is overstated because jadi is also ordinary in Indonesian and menjadi is also ordinary in Malaysian Malay, especially across register and context.
response.cue_rationale: Menjadi and jadi can both mean “become” in the sense of changing into or coming to be.
material_concerns: The pair may mislead learners into treating menjadi as Indonesian-only and jadi as Malaysian-only.

preference_risk.rationale: Both forms are plausibly ordinary in both varieties, with register and contextual differences rather than exclusive national ownership.

response.rationale: Both answers fit “become,” but the proposed contrast is not a reliable country-level distinction: jadi is common in Indonesian, while menjadi remains ordinary in Malaysian Malay. The pair is better framed as a register or contextual preference than a national one.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: The competing forms jadi in Indonesian and menjadi in Malaysian Malay are both ordinary enough to weaken the claimed national contrast.
